answer: Each new agent identity must stake a small bond locked for several epochs, and every attestation it casts draws from that same stake. When a botnet spins up thousands of fresh keys, none carry history, so peers offer only a faint whisper of trust and their votes weigh almost nothing. To buy real weight the attacker must post and forfeit genuine capital per identity, and verified fraud slashes the whole cluster, so the ocean of fake accounts costs more than it earns. A filter like raven is never fooled: one paid stake, one voice.
